claims.text: A solution treatment followed by controlled aging can induce coherent nanoprecipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The induced coherent nanoprecipitates will be nanoscale and uniformly dispersed throughout the alloy matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as efficient sinks for radiation-induced point defects.
Coherent nanoprecipitates capture helium atoms and thereby limit helium-bubble nucleation and growth.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and avoid excessive obstruction of dislocation motion.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could otherwise initiate premature cracking.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can preserve a favorable combination of strength and tensile ductility in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
An additively manufactured, compositionally complex refractory alloy can be produced as the baseline material.
The baseline alloy has a homogeneous microstructure lacking designed secondary phases.
After helium irradiation, the heat-treated alloy will have lower helium-bubble density than the untreated alloy.
After helium irradiation, the heat-treated alloy will have smaller helium bubbles than the untreated alloy.
After irradiation, the heat-treated alloy will retain or improve yield strength relative to the untreated alloy.
After irradiation, the heat-treated alloy will retain or improve ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The beneficial effect requires the precipitates to remain coherent and nanoscale, exemplified by a size below 100 nm.
The precipitate volume fraction must be optimized to avoid excessive hardening and embrittlement.
Insufficient precipitate sink density will reduce the proposed radiation-tolerance benefit.
The proposed effect is intended to hold during elevated-temperature, high-flux helium-ion irradiation simulating fusion conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in helium-bubble size or density, or observation of reduced strength or ductility, would falsify the hypothesis.
